subtitle: Ashoka’s distant whisper, a cave’s thin lines, and the first clear shadow of the fish-bannered south

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a hillside cave above scrubland, with Nedunjeliyan standing silhouetted before it under a sky split between dusk and dawn
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan of Madurai stands in profile before a rock shelter carved with simple stone beds, his fish-bannered spear planted beside him as distant clouds hint at a far northern empire beyond the horizon.

dialogue.text: Centuries before bards sang of Pandya kings, Ashoka’s rock, a cave wall and a far-off war together whisper the first sure name of Madurai’s fish-bannered south.

i18n.hi: कवियों के पांड्य गीतों से सदियों पहले, अशोक की शिला, गुफा की दीवार और दूर का युद्ध मिलकर देते हैं मदुरै के मछली–ध्वज वाले दक्षिण का पहला पक्का नाम।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of the subcontinent with stylized terrain, from the Himalaya to the southern seas
panels.action: A sweeping view shows the Indian subcontinent from snow peaks to palm-fringed coasts, with faint glows marking Pataliputra, Kalinga, and a dim, untitled southern tip beyond the Kaveri and Vaigai rivers.

dialogue.text: In the third century before the Common Era, the Mauryan lion stands over much of the land, but the far south is still a long, dim shape beyond imperial reach.

i18n.hi: ईसा से तीसरी सदी पहले, मौर्य सिंह ज़्यादातर भूभाग पर छाया है, पर सुदूर दक्षिण अभी भी साम्राज्य से परे धुंधला आकार है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on an Ashokan rock edict carved on a rugged boulder in a dry landscape
panels.action: A rugged boulder in a rocky plain bears carefully incised Brahmi letters, its surface sunlit and weathered, with forest and hills receding into haze.

dialogue.text: On such rocks, Ashoka orders his words cut into stone. In Major Rock Edicts Two and Thirteen, he names lands he does not rule, but must still address.

i18n.hi: ऐसी ही चट्टानों पर अशोक अपने शब्द खुदवाता है। प्रमुख शिलालेख दो और तेरह में वह उन भूमि के नाम लिखवाता है जिन पर वह राज नहीं करता, पर जिनसे फिर भी बात करनी है।

panels.shot: tight medium on the inscribed lines with faint superimposed outline of the peninsula’s southern tip in the background
panels.action: The carved lines of the edict stand crisply in close view, while in the background a ghostly outline of the southern peninsula appears, its coastal tips faintly marked.

dialogue.text: Among the Cholas, the Cheras, the Satyaputras and Keralaputras, one more name is cut: the Pandyas, independent, coastal, and important enough to be summoned in stone.

i18n.hi: चोल, चेर, सत्यपुत्र और केरलपुत्र के बीच एक और नाम कटता है: पांड्य, स्वतंत्र, तटीय, और इतना महत्वपूर्ण कि पत्थर पर बुलाया जाए।

panels.shot: documentary-style montage: Ashokan messengers on the road, and imagined Pandya envoys near a southern port
panels.action: Ashokan messengers ride along a dusty road in one frame, while in another, dark-skinned southern envoys stand by a palm-lined harbor, ships at anchor behind them, a subtle visual bridge between north and south.

dialogue.text: These edicts speak of dhamma, compassion and restraint even towards distant peoples. By naming the Pandyas, they prove a polity known and recognised, not mere legend at the end of the map.

i18n.hi: ये शिलालेख धम्म, करुणा और दूर के लोगों पर भी संयम की बात करते हैं। पांड्यों का नाम लेकर वे साबित करते हैं कि यहाँ एक मान्य सत्ता है, नक्शे के छोर की कथा नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Megasthenes at a Greek-style writing desk, with an imaginative painted map behind him
panels.action: A Greek envoy in a long cloak, Megasthenes, sits at a low table, writing on a scroll, while behind him a stylized map shows a southern queenly figure labelled only in Greek imagination.

dialogue.text: Greek writers like Megasthenes will tell of a southern queen called Pandaia, daughter of Heracles. Their stories weave myth, not record; they echo a memory, but cannot guide our steps.

i18n.hi: मेगास्थनीज़ जैसे यूनानी लेखक दक्षिण की रानी पांदैया, हेराक्लीज़ की बेटी, की बातें लिखेंगे। उनकी कथाएँ गाथा हैं, अभिलेख नहीं; वे स्मृति का गुंजन हैं, रास्ता नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of early Madurai settlement with wooden palisades, river beyond, and a modest palace complex
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan walks along a packed-earth street within an early Madurai, where timber palisades, tiled halls, and bustling markets stretch towards a distant river lined with groves.

dialogue.text: South of the Vaigai, in a growing town that will one day be called Madurai, a Pandya court holds council. The king’s name is not yet on stone, but his power is felt along the fish-rich coast.

i18n.hi: वैगई के दक्षिण, बढ़ते नगर में जिसे आगे चलकर मदुरै कहेंगे, एक पांड्य दरबार सभा करता है। राजा का नाम अभी पत्थर पर नहीं, पर उसकी पकड़ मछलियों से भरे तट पर महसूस होती है।

panels.shot: intimate interior medium shot of Nedunjeliyan seated in council with a few chiefs, no lavish throne, simple wooden hall
panels.action: In a simple wooden hall, Nedunjeliyan sits cross-legged on a raised plank among chiefs and elders, weapons stacked against the wall, palm-leaf bundles resting near their feet.

dialogue.text: This early Nedunjeliyan is not yet the hero of later poems. He is a name that will surface beside a cave near Mangulam, tied to men who carve beds for wandering monks.

i18n.hi: यह आरंभिक नेडुंजेलियन अभी कविताओं का नायक नहीं। वह बस एक नाम है जो मंगुलम के पास की गुफा के संग उभरेगा, उन लोगों से जुड़ा जो भिक्षुओं के लिए शय्याएँ काटते हैं।

panels.shot: long shot of Mangulam hill with scrub forest and a small group of workers below
panels.action: A rocky hill rises from thorny scrub near a distant river, its face pocked by shallow caves, while a handful of workers stand below, tools over their shoulders, looking up.

dialogue.text: North of Madurai, near Mangulam, a low hill with natural ledges waits. Here, in the third or second century BCE, hands will cut stone beds beneath the open sky.

i18n.hi: मदुरै के उत्तर, मंगुलम के पास, प्राकृतिक शेल्फ़ों वाली नीची पहाड़ी इंतज़ार करती है। यहीं, तीसरी–दूसरी सदी ईसा पूर्व में, हाथ खुले आसमान तले पत्थर की शय्याएँ काटेंगे।

panels.shot: close-up of artisans chiselling rock-beds under a rock overhang, with two Jain monks watching quietly
panels.action: Artisans kneel under a rock overhang, chiselling flat, raised platforms from the stone, while two shaven-headed Jain monks stand in silence, palms folded, watching the work.

dialogue.text: Early Tamil-Brahmi letters here record donors who prepare these beds for ascetics, likely Jains, seeking shelter from sun and rain as they wander through the Pandya land.

i18n.hi: यहीं की आरंभिक तमिल–ब्राह्मी अक्षरियाँ दानकर्ताओं का लेखा छोड़ती हैं, जो शायद जैन तपस्वियों के लिए ये शय्याएँ बनाते हैं, ताकि वे पांड्य देश में भटकते हुए धूप–बरस से बच सकें।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the Mangulam inscription lines being carved on the rock-bed side
panels.action: The fine point of a chisel traces neat Tamil-Brahmi letters along the side of a stone bed, dust falling from each stroke as the carver leans in with care.

dialogue.text: In one such inscription, later recorded as Mangulam R6 and R7, the donor names are linked by title to a Pandya ruler called Nedunjeliyan, anchoring him in this landscape.

i18n.hi: ऐसे ही एक लेख, जिसे बाद में मंगुलम आर६ और आर७ कहा जाएगा, में दानकर्ताओं के नाम उपाधि के ज़रिए नेडुंजेलियन नामक पांड्य शासक से जुड़ते हैं, उसे इसी भूगोल में जड़ देते हुए।

panels.shot: soft focus on the finished inscription with faint silhouettes of a king, officials, and monks layered behind
panels.action: The completed Tamil-Brahmi inscription stands in sharp focus, while behind it faint silhouettes show a king on a simple dais, officials in discussion, and monks resting on the beds.

dialogue.text: The text does not boast of conquests. It traces a web of patronage: officers serving a Nedunjeliyan, making gifts in his time, in his country, to support renouncers under his watch.

i18n.hi: यह लेख विजयों का घमंड नहीं करता। यह संरक्षा का जाल दिखाता है: नेडुंजेलियन के अधिकारी, उसके समय, उसकी भूमि में, त्यागियों की रक्षा के लिए दान देते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nedunjeliyan at dawn visiting the cave with a small entourage, viewing the rock-beds
panels.action: At dawn, Nedunjeliyan stands quietly at the edge of the Mangulam cave, a few attendants behind him, as he looks down at the smooth stone beds where a monk sleeps, wrapped in a cloth.

dialogue.speaker: the_early_pandya_court_and_nedunjeliyan_i
dialogue.text: Let them rest in our land. Their silence harms no one, and steadies men.

i18n.hi: उन्हें हमारे देश में ठहरने दो। उनकी चुप्पी किसी को नहीं दुखाती, लोगों को थामे रखती है।

panels.shot: low-angle medium close-up of Nedunjeliyan’s face as he listens to a courtier, with faint soundless bustle of Madurai behind
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan’s face fills the frame, thoughtful and alert, as a courtier at the edge of the image leans in, gesturing back toward a distant, busy Madurai street.

dialogue.text: We do not yet know his campaigns or his court songs. We know only that under his name, officials moved, caves were endowed, and a script took shape on stone.

i18n.hi: हम अभी उसके युद्ध या दरबारी गीत नहीं जानते। बस इतना जानते हैं कि उसके नाम के तले अधिकारी चले, गुफाएँ दान हुईं, और पत्थर पर एक लिपि आकार लेने लगी।

panels.shot: transition montage: Mangulam inscription fading into Ashokan edict, then into the Hathigumpha inscription on a cliff
panels.action: The Mangulam letters fade into the Brahmi of an Ashokan edict, which in turn dissolves into the deeply cut lines of the Hathigumpha inscription on a cliff in distant Kalinga.

dialogue.text: Elsewhere, another king’s record will speak of this south. In the Hathigumpha inscription, the Kalinga ruler Kharavela looks across the sea towards a land of pearls and confederate powers.

i18n.hi: कहीं और, दूसरे राजा का लेख भी इस दक्षिण की बात करेगा। हाथीगुम्फा शिलालेख में, कलिंग नरेश खरवेल समुद्र पार मोतियों और संघों की भूमि की ओर नज़र करता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kharavela on a balcony overlooking a harbour with ships, imagining distant southern coasts
panels.action: Kharavela stands on a stone balcony above a busy harbor, wind tugging at his cloak, as he gazes toward the misty line of the sea where ships slip toward the southern horizon.

dialogue.text: Kharavela’s text boasts of reaching the Tamil land and of pearls from the Pandya coast. Across the Bay of Bengal, the wealth of these fisheries has become a line in another king’s self-praise.

i18n.hi: खरवेल का लेख तमिल देश तक पहुँचने और पांड्य तट के मोतियों पर गर्व करता है। बंगाल की खाड़ी के पार, इन मत्स्य–केंद्रों की दौलत एक और राजा की आत्म–स्तुति की पंक्ति बन जाती है।

panels.shot: evocative wide shot of divers leaping from a boat into clear coastal waters, with heaps of oysters on another boat
panels.action: Bare-bodied divers plunge from a wooden boat into bright coastal waters, while on another boat heaps of oysters glisten in the sun and a supervisor counts baskets on deck.

dialogue.text: We can see the scene behind the words: divers in the Pandya Gulf, bringing up oysters, merchants weighing pearls, and distant courts measuring the south by what it can send.

i18n.hi: हम इन शब्दों के पीछे का दृश्य देख सकते हैं: पांड्य खाड़ी में गोताखोर, सीपी उठाते, व्यापारी मोती तौलते, और दूर–दराज दरबार दक्षिण को उसकी भेजी दौलत से नापते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nedunjeliyan in a modest court, a trader presenting a small casket, map of coastlines scratched on the floor
panels.action: In the Pandya hall, a coastal trader kneels and opens a small wooden casket of pearls before Nedunjeliyan, while on the packed-earth floor a simple map of rivers and inlets has been scratched with a stick.

dialogue.speaker: the_early_pandya_court_and_nedunjeliyan_i
dialogue.text: Guard the mouths of our rivers. The sea is our field; pearls, our harvest.

i18n.hi: नदियों के मुहानों की रखवाली करो। समुद्र हमारा खेत है, मोती हमारी फ़सल।

panels.shot: reflective shot: a scholar in a modern archive studying estampages of Ashokan, Mangulam, and Hathigumpha inscriptions side by side
panels.action: A modern scholar in a quiet archive bends over three inked estampages laid side by side—Ashoka’s edict, the Mangulam inscription, and Hathigumpha—light from a window falling across the papers.

dialogue.text: Today, epigraphers like Iravatham Mahadevan read these thin, scattered lines with care, placing scripts in sequence and refusing to stretch them into certainty they cannot bear.

i18n.hi: आज इरावतम महादेवन जैसे शिलालेख–विद अपने–अपने ये पतली, बिखरी पंक्तियाँ सावधानी से पढ़ते हैं, लिपियों को क्रम में रखते हैं, और उन्हें उन निश्चितताओं तक खींचने से इनकार करते हैं जिन्हें वे उठा नहीं सकतीं।

panels.shot: melancholic wide shot of Mangulam hill at sunset, Nedunjeliyan’s translucent figure fading into the rock
panels.action: At sunset, Mangulam hill glows red while the faint, translucent figure of Nedunjeliyan stands before the cave and slowly merges into the rock face, leaving only the inscription.

dialogue.text: The legend of three great Sangams will be woven much later. Here, in this early age, we have no full court-chronicle—only rock, script and the shadow of a king behind a donor’s name.

i18n.hi: तीनों महान संगमों की कथा बहुत बाद में बुनी जाएगी। यहाँ, इस आरंभिक युग में, हमारे पास कोई पूरा दरबार–इतिहास नहीं—बस चट्टान, लिपि और एक दाता के नाम के पीछे छुपी राजा की परछाई।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of Nedunjeliyan’s hand touching the rock-bed edge, seamlessly matched to a modern hand tracing the same inscription
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan’s hand rests on the edge of a freshly cut rock-bed; in the same position, the image shifts into a modern researcher’s hand tracing the now-aged inscription grooves.

dialogue.text: Fragments like Ashoka’s edict, Mangulam’s cave and Hathigumpha’s boast cannot map a Pandya empire, but they prove a real beginning—the first fish carved clearly enough to outlast memory.

i18n.hi: अशोक के शिलालेख, मंगुलम की गुफा और हाथीगुम्फा के गर्व जैसे टुकड़े पांड्य साम्राज्य का नक्शा नहीं बनाते, पर वे असली आरंभ साबित करते हैं—पहली मछली जो स्मृति के बाद भी साफ़ कटी रह गई।

subtitle_i18n.en: Ashoka’s distant whisper, a cave’s thin lines, and the first clear shadow of the fish-bannered south
subtitle_i18n.hi: अशोक की दूर की फुसफुसाहट, गुफा की पतली रेखाएँ, और मछली–ध्वज वाले दक्षिण की पहली साफ परछाई
